title: Grove: Press for Light
intro: A Grove button and a Grove LED: press the button to light it up, then make it remember whether it's on or off.

steps.title: Read the button
steps.text:
A Grove button reads **1 (HIGH) while it's pressed** and **0 (LOW)** when it isn't. (A breadboard button with `INPUT_PULLUP` is the other way round: the Grove button has its own resistor.)

**Your task:** press **Run**, open the **Serial Monitor**, and press the button. Watch the numbers.
hints: In the simulator, click and hold the Grove button.
The Serial Monitor is under the code.
Hold it down for a moment so a few 1s appear.

checks.label: I saw 1 when I pressed the button

steps.success: The board can feel your button press.

steps.title: Light while pressed
steps.text:
`if` lets your program decide. If the button reads HIGH, turn the LED on. Otherwise (`else`), turn it off.

**Your task:** fill in the two comments with `digitalWrite` lines.
hints: One line goes under each comment.

checks.label: The LED lights while you press
The LED goes off when you let go

steps.success: Your LED follows the button: a tiny bit of decision-making.

steps.title: Remember on or off
steps.text:
**Goal:** make each press **switch** the light: press once for on, again for off. Print "on" or "off" each time.

You'll need a `bool` variable to remember, `!` to flip it, and a little wait until the button is let go (or one press would flip it many times).
hints: When pressed: `lightOn = !lightOn;` then set the LED to match.
After that, wait in `while (digitalRead(BUTTON_PIN) == HIGH) { delay(10); }`
steps.success: That's a toggle switch, like a desk lamp's.

outro: You used **digitalRead**, **if / else** and a **variable** to make a Grove button control a light.
stretch: Make a long press (over 1 second) turn the light on for 10 seconds.
Count presses and print the count.
Add a second Grove LED on D7 that lights while the first is off.
